newsitem.title: UK: Producer group wants USDA to explain coffee data.
newsitem.headline: Producer group wants USDA to explain coffee data.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said on Tuesday it would welcome clarification from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) over methodology of its latest coffee supply estimates.
The ACPC said its members were concerned over the USDA forecast which it said differed vastly from the recent production number released by some governments.
The USDA put Brazil's 1996/97 and 1997/98 coffee crops at 27.5 million and 28 million bags respectively.
This compares with the Brazilian government estimates of 25-26 million and 22 million respectively, the London-based ACPC said.
"We would also note that the USDA forecast appears to be the only forecast in the market that goes against the consensus of a production drop this year," the 14-member group said.

Indonesia recently reduced their own forecast to 4.83 million bags, compared with the USDA estimate of 6.8 million and Colombian production is estimated at 12-15 million by the Coffee Growers Federation, compared with 11.3 million estimated by the USDA, an ACPC statement said.
"Members have also expressed concerns that forecasts for some non-member countries also appear to be very high," it added.
"The ACPC would welcome clarification from the USDA over methodology of these estimates..." it said.
It said an USDA clarification would assist all market participants "in forming the best possible judgements of prospects for the market".
"The ACPC is in no way critical of independent forecasts as such, and indeed continues to encourage this principle," the statement added.
The USDA estimate for Brazil's 1997/98 crop has stunned traders in the country and prompted the country's top coffee official to describe it as ludricrous.
